summary.headline: Mold-Tek Q4 FY26 PAT turned to INR 2.28 crore from a loss, but FY26 PAT fell 17% to INR 10 crore on a INR 4 crore FX MTM hit.
summary.overview: Management reported a Q4 FY26 profit of INR 2.28 crore versus a loss of about INR 1.6 crore a year earlier, despite a roughly INR 4 crore MTM loss from rupee depreciation on forward contracts. Full-year PAT was about INR 10 crore against INR 12.16 crore in FY25, with management citing EBITDA of about INR 20 crore standalone (INR 19.64 crore consolidated) against INR 23 crore a year earlier. Beryl, acquired in November 2025, contributed five months of revenue, and the MES automobile (BIW) team was cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March. Management reiterated plans to move into structural design and targets of INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin for FY27. Analyst questions were pointed on EBITDA definition, the cancelled preferential issue, receivables and hedging, and several figures were disputed or left for follow-up with the CFO.

segments.name: Civil / Structural (steel detailing and design, India-based, US clients)
segments.commentary: Work on hand grew from about $4 million at start of FY26 to about $5 million at end-March 2026, which management described as growth of about 60-70% versus $2.84 million in June 2024. Structural design is about 10% of civil revenue, versus nearly 0% three to four years ago. Management targets 30-40% of revenue from design in three to four years.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical Engineering Services) - BIW automobile
segments.commentary: Team cut from about 160 to 60 people by end-March; the team was closed from April 1. The segment lost about INR 7-8 crore a year and about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 FY26. Work on hand fell from about $0.5 million in Q1 to about $0.25 million.

segments.name: MES - Poles, towers and substation (US)
segments.commentary: Team grew from 45-50 to about 80 people. FY26 revenue was about $0.8 million; management expects FY27 to cross $1.5-2 million. Around 80-90% of this work comes from the USA.

segments.name: Beryl (US residential structural design, inspection and permitting; acquired Nov 2025)
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 80% permitting/inspection and 20% design. Team of about 40 in Tampa with no resignations in five months. Management guided Beryl margin at 8-10% for FY27 and said it can grow to about $5-7 million with India design support.

segments.name: PEMB (Pre-Engineering Metal Buildings)
segments.commentary: Now about 5% of revenue, down from being the core business before 2010.

segments.name: New MSA with Danieli Corus (Delhi, MES manpower)
segments.commentary: Mandate for 20 people; 3 fulfilled so far. Contract period 1-3 years, potential about $0.5 million per annum within a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 250 crore, with management saying INR 240 crore is 'easily feasible' from the Q4 run-rate of INR 59 crore (times four).
EBITDA margin to move from about 11% to at least 15%.
Standalone engineering business (MES plus civil from India) expected to grow at least 15-20%, with EBITDA margin in the 15-16% region.
MES cost cut expected to add about INR 7-8 crore back to profitability; productivity target improvement of at least 20% in FY27 (10-15% gain claimed in April).
Nashik office move expected to save about INR 2-2.5 crore per year from FY28; building targeted to be ready by end of FY27.
Hedging policy to be limited to 25-50% of turnover (previously up to 100%); operational EBITDA to be reported separately from MTM gains and losses from FY27.
Salary hike of 8.5-9% provided in Q4 for Indian teams; Beryl not yet covered.
capex_capacity: Team of 40-45 structural designers in India plus 2-3 in the USA; a 6-member Indian team was created for Beryl, with a plan for a 15-20 person India team, targeted by Q4 FY27.
Nashik owned building site acquired a couple of years ago; municipal approvals expected by end of May, ground work in June, completion by end FY27.
Management is in talks for an acquisition of a high-rise steel structural design company; one target is near the Atlanta office. No deal concluded.
Two PEs (professional engineers) certified in more than 20 US states; PE support needed for full member design.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand up to about $5 million at end-March 2026, against about $4 million at start of the year (per Q4 opening remarks); Q&A figure of $2.5 million at start of year.
Pricing: projects quoted on a fixed-price basis at about $30/hour in India, with 2-3% negotiation; structural design rates about $70-80 per hour versus $25-30 for detailing.
Trade uncertainty between the US and India has stalled Interarch and Mold-Tek building orders in the US; no revenue progress from Interarch or Affordable Robotic Partnership.
BIW automobile demand fell as EV adoption and new model launches slowed; European work was over 50% of MES, while poles and towers are 80-90% US.
Beryl order book estimated at $0.2-0.3 million at any time, maximum about $0.5 million (per management; to be checked).

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 INR 250 crore revenue and 15% EBITDA margin realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 240 crore is easily feasible from Q4 revenue of INR 59 crore annualised, and that margin should rise from 11% to at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 2.9 lakh preferential issue at INR 164 cancelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the investor did not transfer funds because the share price had fallen to about INR 130, so the issue lapsed on 30 April against a 31 May deadline. The issue was independent of the Beryl stake purchase. About 30% of acquisition money is held as a three-year retention guarantee.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation hit P&L when costs are mainly wages, and what is the hedging policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Forwards booked at INR 85-92 led to about INR 4.9 crore MTM loss in Q4 as rupee moved to about INR 95. Management is cutting hedge cover to 25-50% of turnover and will show MTM separately from operational EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables doubled and revenue rose only about 40%; is the standalone business weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 turnover rose 81% YoY, that the rise in debtors reflects this growth, and that acquisitions are strategic rather than a response to weakness. It cited zero debt and INR 25-30 crore of deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MES loss and when does it end?
qa_highlights.answer: The MES loss was about INR 1.7-1.9 crore in Q4 and about INR 7-8 crore a year; management said the team was closed from 1 April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What were Beryl's revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl did INR 22.9 crore in the five months since acquisition, including INR 11 crore in Q4 with a loss of about INR 70 lakh. Management said Beryl's seasonal Q4 is typically weak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Danieli Corus MSA and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: A manpower MSA in MES with a mandate for 20 people (3 deployed so far), a contract period of 1-3 years, and potential of about $0.5 million per year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 Florida SB 4-D inspection tailwind at Beryl ending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first inspection phase is complete and payments received; the second design phase was delayed by a government shutdown and is now restarting, so the tailwind is mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the threat from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI has a limited role in design and detailing, may cut headcount by 5-10% through checking tasks, and that back charges are zero.

risks_watch: MTM exposure on forward contracts: management said Q1 FY27 MTM losses would be a few lakhs at rupee near 95.5 versus INR 4 crore in Q4; watch whether hedging cut to 25-50% of turnover and MTM shown separately from operational EBITDA.

Beryl execution: five-month revenue INR 22.9 crore but Q4 loss about INR 70 lakh; Q4 is seasonally weak, and the Florida SB 4-D design phase was delayed by a government shutdown and is only restarting.
MES downsizing: team cut from about 160 to 60 and MES closed from 1 April; verify the INR 7-8 crore annual loss stops and that no residual BIW revenue is lost.
Receivables rose from about INR 30 crore (September) to INR 41 crore (March) while management attributed the rise to growth; watch debtor days and collections.
FY27 targets (INR 250 crore revenue, 15% EBITDA margin) rest on Q4 run-rate annualised and a 60-70% civil order-book increase; watch quarterly civil order book (about $5 million) and conversion.

Unresolved figures: EBITDA disputed (INR 20 crore vs analyst's INR 10.5 crore), order-book split and Beryl order book (to be checked), and other expenses breakup deferred to CFO; the cancelled INR 4.75 crore preferential issue and lock-in for Beryl seller are open items.
key_quotes: I am very glad to inform you that there is a good turnaround in Q4.
So, multiplying by 4, you will see INR 240 crores is easily feasible.
Not even a single person resigned from the 40-member team.
So, the company is planning to adopt the same from this current financial year.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on Q4 turnaround, FY27 targets and MES cost cuts, but defensive when pressed on EBITDA definition, receivables and the cancelled preferential issue. It deferred several figures to the CFO and called out that it had not yet tracked some Beryl order book details.

Beryl India design team: 6 now, plan for 15-20 people, targeted by Q4 FY27

growth.why: FY27 revenue target ~INR 250 cr (about 31% over FY26 implied by ~INR 190 cr base, not stated directly) with EBITDA margin to 15%+; backed partly by Q4 run-rate of INR 59 cr (x4 = INR 236-240 cr), civil work on hand ~$5 mn (up 60-70%), MES cost cut worth INR 7-8 cr, and poles/towers to $1.5-2 mn, but no new productive capacity is being added and US trade uncertainty has stalled Interarch orders.
